description: Proposed single storey rear extension, basement extension with front and rear lightwells.
decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the basement extension and lightwell against groundwater flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the basement extension is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with BS 8102:2022 Protection of below ground structures against water ingress - code of practice.</p><p>Reason: To ensure the property is protected against flood risks from groundwater.&nbsp;</p>

<p>Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp; maintenance plan of at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (i.e. water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume.</p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-6051c83e-7fff-3dea-14c2-d2b0cb040e29"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">Reason: To mitigate against the impacts of surface water flooding.</span></span></p>

<p>All new external facing and roofing materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works carried out in this connection) shall match those of the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance including type, size, colour, bond, pointing, coursing, jointing, profile and texture, notwithstanding the details provided in the approved plans.&nbsp;</p><p>

REASON:&nbsp;To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and does not detract from the character and visual amenity of the area.</p>

<div>Within 1 month of the completion of the development hereby approved, the applicant shall provide adequate evidence of installed hedgehog access holes along the boundary fencing. The evidence shall include: A minimum of 1 Hedgehog Hole where a wall or fence is to be used as the boundary treatment, with such hole meeting the standards, unless that boundary is directly adjacent to a public road with no meaningful verge or footpath. Each hole must be at ground level and must create a gap through the fence or wall of approx. 13cm wide and 13cm high. Larger holes to be avoided. Each hole must have an appropriate sign near to the hole to educate on the purpose of the hole e.g. small sign would the words "Hedgehog highway - please keep open". The hole should not be located near drains or other wet areas, no any area which would require a hedgehog to 'step up' to reach it.&nbsp;</div><div><br></div><div>REASON: To support and preserve endangered urban biodiversity by providing habitats.</div><div><br style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"></div>
